name: DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inc.
moat_justification: US scale leader with vendor allocation leverage, House of Sport and GameChanger differentiators and a ~30M-member loyalty base, but the brands own the product and the pricing power: Nike sells direct, Amazon/TJX pressure price, gross margin is thin and falling (35.9% FY2025 to 32.9% FY2026 to 32.1% TTM), and the acquired Foot Locker chain is a Nike-dependent mall asset with negative comps. ROIC proxy history is unusable as moat evidence (absurd pre-deal prints on a near-zero funded-debt capital base; 19.5% in the first post-deal year).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 5.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 3.25 vs 3-yr median 5.28 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
one_liner: Strong core retailer, moat 4/10, that bought a broken Foot Locker — at $144.35 it does not clear 15% on any defensible base (weighted IRR 6.8%, IV@15% $48.63); it would need to fall to ~$49 to clear the hurdle.
moat_for: US sporting-goods scale leader — buying leverage and vendor (Nike) allocations
House of Sport experiential format and GameChanger youth-sports platform
~30M-member ScoreCard loyalty base and DICK'S Media Network
Core comps +4.9% in Q2 FY2027 into a promotional market — share-taking
moat_against: Brands own the product and pricing power; Nike DTC and allocation control
Amazon and off-price (TJX) competition with no structural cost answer
Gross margin thin and falling: 35.9% to 32.9% to 32.1% TTM on promotions and Foot Locker mix
Foot Locker: mall-based, Nike-dependent, pro forma comps -3.6% and segment operating loss
